title: Unify GPU pool lifecycle & allocation responsibilities; clean capacity planner technical debt
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: The capacity planner and node lifecycle code paths have drifted over the last 18 months: multiple teams have added shortcut mutations on Node objects, ad-hoc allocation heuristics live in the autoscaler controller, and the k8s client library is two major versions behind. This has caused brittle scale-down interactions and three subtle outages during burst tests. Goal: consolidate lifecycle responsibilities into a single NodeManager abstraction, remove direct Node mutations from the capacity planner, upgrade the k8s client to v0.27.x, and clean up allocation heuristics so they are testable and benchmarked. Scope: refactor capacity planner internals, introduce NodeManager interface (in-memory and k8s-backed implementations), migrate allocation tests to use deterministic fixtures, bump k8s client, and add integration tests and benchmarks. Out of scope: changing scheduling policy or autoscaler scaling algorithm (this will be a follow-up), changes to node image or driver installs. Why now: ongoing incidents and upcoming Dedicated capacity launch require predictable lifecycle behavior and safer rollouts. Success metrics: fewer scale-down races (incidents reduced), improved CI integration test coverage, and no regressions in 95th percentile scale-up latency after migration.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity planner no longer performs direct Node object mutations; NodeManager handles all node lifecycle operations
Integration test suite that simulates 50 concurrent allocation requests passes in CI on the canary cluster
95th percentile scale-up latency stays within 1.5x of pre-refactor baseline in the benchmark harness
All PRs receive code-owner approvals and pass e2e + canary rollout monitoring with automatic rollback configured
Documentation updated: design doc, runbook, and console incident dashboard links added
comments: 2026-03-01 – Aisha Kapoor: Spikes completed last week showed two primary root causes: (1) capacity planner mutating k8s Node labels concurrently with the autoscaler controller, (2) stale backoff timers. Decided to extract NodeManager to centralize API calls and backoff state.
2026-03-02 – Daniel Morales: Prototype NodeManager implemented (in-memory + kube backed). Local unit tests pass. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4127

2026-03-04 – Lila Chen (SRE): Ran canary burst test against prototype; observed fewer label-flapping events but a small regression in scale-up latency due to additional RPCs. Suggest adding batching for node annotation writes and metric instrumentation before canary rollout.

2026-03-05 – Daniel Morales: Added batching to NodeManager write path and switched to client-go v0.27.1 in go.mod. Benchmarks: median unchanged, 95th improved by ~3% compared to baseline. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4142

2026-03-07 – Priya Nair (Platform Eng): Code review comments: please add clear ownership boundaries in the comments and a migration checklist. Also asked for a migration feature flag for the rollout to Dedicated clusters.

2026-03-09 – Aisha Kapoor: Migration plan drafted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/NodeManager+Migration. Added canary to two non-production clusters and a rollback window. Assigned follow-ups for runbook updates and alerting thresholds.
